parcel.name: Demo Parcel A — Columbia Basin (FICTIONAL)
parcel.engagement: Sample engagement — fictional parcel assembled to demonstrate the deliverable format; every fact and source on this report is invented.

recommendation: Proceed to PSA, with closing conditioned on (1) recordation of an amended, corridor-confined transmission easement resolving title-1 — this is the single go/no-go item; (2) a written will-serve letter superseding the study-queue acknowledgment (power-2); and (3) rollback-tax allocation to seller (title-5). The watch items are manageable in the ordinary course; the wildlife survey window (environmental-3) should drive the grading schedule now, not at permit time.

power-1.finding: Parcel lies entirely within Grant County PUD's exclusive service territory; no territory overlap with adjacent co-op.
sources: [fictional sample] Grant County PUD service-territory map; WUTC territory registry, reviewed 2026-06-08

power-2.finding: PUD load study (in progress) indicates 75 MW available 2028, 150 MW contingent on a planned 230kV substation expansion; no will-serve letter yet — only a study-queue acknowledgment.
sources: [fictional sample] Grant County PUD large-load study acknowledgment letter dated 2026-04-30

power-3.finding: PUD evolving-industry rate schedule applies: 15-year minimum-take term with collateral posting; a pending rate proceeding could raise the demand charge ~12%.
sources: [fictional sample] Grant County PUD Schedule 17 (evolving industries); open rate docket reviewed 2026-06-08

power-4.finding: Existing 230kV BPA line traverses the section 0.8 miles north; PUD substation with documented headroom 1.6 miles east.
sources: [fictional sample] BPA transmission map overlay; PUD system map, reviewed 2026-06-08

power-5.finding: No third-party interconnection queue rights marketed with the land; service is distribution-level via PUD, avoiding BPA cluster-study exposure at this scale.
sources: [fictional sample] Seller diligence responses; BPA queue search, reviewed 2026-06-08

power-6.finding: No behind-the-meter generation contemplated at this scale; county is in attainment for NOx/ozone, preserving the option for backup-gen permitting.
sources: [fictional sample] Ecology air-quality attainment designations, reviewed 2026-06-08

power-7.finding: Substation expansion CIAC is estimated at $18-24M, due in two tranches before energization; refund mechanism if capacity later shared is capped at 50%.
sources: [fictional sample] PUD facilities-charge estimate dated 2026-05-15

power-8.finding: Schedule 17 service is firm; curtailment limited to system emergencies under standard tariff terms.
sources: [fictional sample] Grant County PUD Schedule 17 tariff text, reviewed 2026-06-08

zoning-1.finding: Zoned Rural Heavy Industrial; 'data center / server farm' is a permitted use by right under GCC 23.08 use table.
sources: [fictional sample] Grant County Code Title 23 use matrix, reviewed 2026-06-08

zoning-2.finding: No moratorium pending in Grant County, but a neighboring county adopted a 6-month data center moratorium in March 2026 — contagion risk at the county commission is real but not imminent.
sources: [fictional sample] County commission minutes Jan-May 2026; regional press review, reviewed 2026-06-08

zoning-3.finding: Washington vests development rights at complete building-permit application; PSA closing conditioned on permit-application acceptance.
sources: [fictional sample] RCW 19.27.095 vesting doctrine; PSA draft sec. 6.2, reviewed 2026-06-08

zoning-4.finding: No data-center-specific noise or screening standards in current code; nearest residential receptor is 1.4 miles, beyond the 60 dBA contour of a standard generator yard layout.
sources: [fictional sample] GCC ch. 8.68 noise; aerial measurement, reviewed 2026-06-08

zoning-5.finding: By-right use means site-plan review only — administrative, no public hearing; SEPA checklist is the only discretionary touchpoint.
sources: [fictional sample] Grant County development-review flowchart, reviewed 2026-06-08

zoning-6.finding: No proffer regime; recent comparable approvals carried only standard road-impact fees (~$1.1M at this scale).
sources: [fictional sample] County fee schedule; two recent comparable site-plan files, reviewed 2026-06-08

water-1.finding: Closed-loop design: peak demand 110 gpm, average 38 gpm; city industrial main extension 0.9 miles with purveyor capacity letter sized to peak day.
sources: [fictional sample] Purveyor capacity letter dated 2026-05-20; basis-of-design memo

water-2.finding: No new appropriation needed; service is municipal. Parcel's stale 1962 irrigation right is being relinquished by seller at closing.
sources: [fictional sample] Ecology water-rights query; PSA sec. 5.8, reviewed 2026-06-08

water-3.finding: Blowdown volumes from closed-loop design within POTW pretreatment thresholds; no industrial discharge permit required at design loads.
sources: [fictional sample] POTW pretreatment coordinator email dated 2026-05-22

water-4.finding: Closed-loop design makes reclaimed supply immaterial; nearest purple-pipe main is 7 miles and unbudgeted.

environmental-1.finding: Phase I ESA found no RECs; historical use is dryland wheat. PFAS and orchard-chemical non-scope items addressed — no orchard history on the parcel.
sources: [fictional sample] Phase I ESA, ABC Environmental, dated 2026-05-01

environmental-2.finding: NWI mapping and field reconnaissance show no jurisdictional waters on the buildable area; one roadside ditch determined non-jurisdictional.
sources: [fictional sample] Wetland reconnaissance memo dated 2026-04-22

environmental-3.finding: Site is mapped shrub-steppe; ground-nesting bird surveys required March-June. Grading start before July 1 risks a season slip if surveys find occupied habitat.
sources: [fictional sample] WDFW PHS data review; biologist memo dated 2026-05-05

environmental-4.finding: Attainment area; 24 x 3MW diesel units pencil as a synthetic-minor source with standard permitting (~8 months).
sources: [fictional sample] Air permitting feasibility memo dated 2026-05-10

environmental-5.finding: Zone X (outside floodplain); geotech borings show dense gravels, groundwater >60 ft; standard spread footings feasible.
sources: [fictional sample] FEMA FIRM panel; preliminary geotech report dated 2026-04-28

title-1.finding: Schedule B-II discloses a blanket transmission easement (1948, undefined location) in favor of the PUD's predecessor across the entire section — as written it permits future lines anywhere on the parcel. PUD has indicated willingness to confine to a defined corridor, but until an amended easement is recorded this is a no-go condition for a mission-critical pad.
sources: [fictional sample] Title commitment, Schedule B-II item 14, eff. 2026-05-18

title-2.finding: Mineral estate never severed; chain of title confirms surface and minerals united since patent.

title-3.finding: ALTA survey overlays show the conceptual substation yard clipping a 30-ft irrigation-district lateral easement; relocation agreement with the district is feasible but unpriced.
sources: [fictional sample] ALTA survey dated 2026-05-25, overlay vs. concept plan

title-5.finding: Parcel is in open-space ag classification since 2009; conversion triggers ~$410K rollback plus penalty. PSA currently silent on allocation — needs a buyer-favorable allocation or price adjustment.
sources: [fictional sample] County assessor classification record; rollback estimate, reviewed 2026-06-08

tax-1.finding: Washington data center sales/use tax exemption available in this county (rural county program); eligibility window and 40-job covenant are achievable at planned scale, but certification must precede equipment purchase orders.
sources: [fictional sample] RCW 82.08 data center exemption program materials, reviewed 2026-06-08

tax-2.finding: Servers and generators classified as personal property; county has no special data-center assessment history. No local abatement needed under current pro forma.
sources: [fictional sample] County assessor personal-property guidance, reviewed 2026-06-08

tax-3.finding: No negotiated incentive agreement contemplated; statutory exemption only.

tax-4.finding: Straight asset purchase; REET applies at standard graduated rates — controlling-interest structure evaluated and rejected (no material savings on these facts).
sources: [fictional sample] REET calculation memo, reviewed 2026-06-08

tax-5.finding: Parcel is unincorporated — no city utility tax; annexation risk low (nearest city UGA boundary 4.2 miles, no expansion in current comp plan cycle).
sources: [fictional sample] County comp plan UGA map, reviewed 2026-06-08

fiber-1.finding: One long-haul route parallels the BPA corridor at the section line; the second diverse path requires a 6-mile lateral along county ROW — feasible, ~$2.1M, 9-month construct.
sources: [fictional sample] Carrier route maps (two carriers); lateral cost estimate dated 2026-05-19

fiber-2.finding: County franchise process for fiber laterals is administrative (60-90 days); no railroad crossings on either contemplated path.
sources: [fictional sample] County public-works franchise checklist, reviewed 2026-06-08

fiber-3.finding: Target tenant is AI training; latency to IXPs not a leasing prerequisite per client's basis of design.

political-1.finding: No organized opposition in Grant County to date, but regional press tone turned critical in Q1 2026 and a citizens' group is active in the adjacent county; recommend community-engagement plan before site-plan submission.
sources: [fictional sample] Local press review Jan-Jun 2026; planning-commission minutes, reviewed 2026-06-08

political-2.finding: Two bills carried over in the legislature touching the data center exemption (performance reporting; ratepayer-protection conditions on large-load tariffs). Neither passed; both expected back next session.
sources: [fictional sample] Legislative bill tracking, 2026 session review, 2026-06-08

political-3.finding: No land-use appeal history on industrial approvals in this county in the past 5 years; PUD's large-load proceedings uncontested to date.
sources: [fictional sample] GMHB and superior-court docket search, reviewed 2026-06-08

political-4.finding: County commission seats are not up until next year; no candidate has made data centers an issue. Administrative approval path further insulates timing.
sources: [fictional sample] County election calendar; press review, reviewed 2026-06-08
